A run can be driven on a chosen **harness config**: the harness, model, effort and speed tier every case of a dataset runs on, set with harbor agent kwargs on `just minds-evals-run`. Together with the (mngr, dwt) pair the dataset was generated from, it makes up the trial's **arm** -- the whole treatment a result is read at. `--ak lane=` picks the provider lane the workspace signs in on and with it the harness (`anthropic` for claude, and `api-key`, `openrouter` or `opencode-go` for pi-coding); `--ak model=` and `--ak effort=` switch the chat to a catalog id before turn 1, and `--ak fast=` sets the speed tier. The default is the `anthropic` lane with no switch at all, so a run line that passes no harness flags drives the product exactly as it ships. `model` without `effort`, `fast` without `model`, `key_provider` off the `api-key` lane, and `--ak proxy=true` off the `anthropic` lane are all refused when the driver is constructed, before a box boots. The dataset is untouched by the harness config, so every config run against a dataset shares its one image build and one generation.

The workspace's key is read from the variable `--ak key_env=` names, derived from the lane when it is left unset: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` on `anthropic`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on `openrouter`, and `<KEY_PROVIDER>_API_KEY` on `api-key`. Name the variable explicitly where the template does not follow that pattern (`google` reads `GEMINI_API_KEY`) and on the `opencode-go` lane, which has no derived default. A variable that is unset stops the run at construction, naming the variable and the lane. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is required whatever the arm: the decider, the judges and the UI-flow agent are the harness's own spend and do not change with it.

The model switch is applied after the workspace's first chat has answered its `/welcome` greeting, because nothing a client sends can decline that greeting and a switch typed into its window would race the delivery. The greeting therefore always runs on the workspace's default model in the template's speed tier; it shows up as its own `per_model` row in `usage.json`, named by `arm.harness_config.welcome_model`, and a reader comparing arms subtracts it. A stepped case prepares its workspace once, so its harness config is applied once and every step records the same arm.

Every trial records an `arm` block in `state.json`, in the trajectory's `extra.minds_evals` and in the trial metadata: the `mngr_sha` and `dwt_sha` the box was built from and the workspace was cloned from, and a nested `harness_config` carrying the lane and key provider, the account id, the `harness` read back from the workspace's own accounts listing, the requested `model`, `effort` and `fast`, a `model_choice_switch` field reading `applied` or `skipped` or what stopped it, the models actually observed in the transcript, and `is_model_confirmed` -- true when exactly one model was observed and it is the requested one under the harness's own naming, and `null` rather than false for a catalog id the naming table cannot translate into a reported name or for a trial whose transcript says nothing about the model it ran on. A trial that silently ran on the wrong model is therefore visible from the record, and `minds-evals check-run` fails such a trial outright: a trial that asked for a model and recorded `is_model_confirmed: false` fails with a reason naming the model requested and the ones it answered on, while `null` stays neutral. The check-run summaries carry the harness half of the arm too -- an `arm` column in the markdown table beside the mngr and dwt columns, and `lane`, `requested_model`, `is_model_confirmed` and `wrong_model_reason` per trial in the JSON. A harness config's own failures name it in `timed_out_reason` the way the other preparation failures do, including the endpoint's own detail when it refuses a catalog id.

Trials on a harness other than claude are graded without `harness_quality`. The report its judges score is built by claude-shaped rules -- a skill invocation is the `Skill` tool, and two of its six failure signatures name claude's own skill and plugin vocabulary -- so on a pi-coding trajectory it comes out thin for want of those rules rather than for want of friction, and a judge told that an empty report is a sound harness returns a false pass. The verifier reads the harness from the trajectory's `agent.name`, skips the judge, and stamps a `harness` block on `reward-details.json` naming what ran and saying the dimension did not apply. The reward composition drops that share rather than redistributing it (`reward = gates_all_passed ? earned : 0`), so `reward` keeps the same range and the same meaning on every arm. A trial whose transcript could not be captured takes its harness from the recorded arm instead, since the fallback trajectory names the driver in `agent.name`. Both grade-time renderers also read pi-coding's lowercase `bash` as a shell tool, so what it printed reaches the judged transcript's progress timeline and the harness report the way claude's `Bash` output does.

`configs/eval-config-probe.json` is a new checked-in config: one case, one literal turn asking the agent to name the model it is running as, and no expectations. It is the cheapest way to check that a lane or a harness config works end to end.

**Scores are not comparable across arms.** An arm changes the system under test in either half: a run with `fast=false` is not comparable to one that left the template's fast mode on, and a pi-coding run is not comparable to a claude run on any dimension but cost. Two arms that differ in both their pair and their harness config attribute nothing to either, so vary one at a time, and version or flag result sets at the arm.

The async ratchet exempts the files whose async surface harbor's interfaces force -- the driver, the minds bridge, the evidence collector, and the tests and mock environment that drive them -- so its recorded count tracks only the async this project chooses, and adding a test that exercises one more trial does not move it.
